title: The billing PR added a PATCH /api/subscription endpoint that takes the target customer's email from a query parameter instead of the logged-in user, so any authenticated user can cancel or resume anyone's Stripe subscription.

findings.explanation: No SQL injection vulnerabilities detected. All database queries use Django ORM with parameterized filters (e.g., Subscription.objects.filter(user__email=email)) which are safe against SQL injection. The email parameter is passed through the ORM's filter method, not concatenated into raw SQL.

Authorization checks appear adequate. The functions operate on email-based lookup and user context. The get_user_subscription and set_user_subscription functions filter by email and only modify the associated user's subscription. Database queries consistently filter by the user object or user__email, which establishes proper ownership context. No IDOR vulnerability is evident in this diff as object fetches are tied to authenticated user context through email lookup.
findings.suggested_fix: Ensure that when these functions are called from endpoints, the email parameter is derived from the authenticated user context (not user-supplied) and that the user parameter passed to EntryAdapters methods is the currently authenticated user, not a user-controlled value.
